decisions.reason: Adding bathroom-door edge-offset annotations documents the existing layout but does not change Unit 2 bathroom placement, plumbing, or door position.
The annotation request does not resolve or modify the Unit 1 en-suite arrangement, fixture fit, or existing value ambiguity.
The source requests dimension annotations on the plan and does not require those annotations on the separate furnished drawing.
Door edge-offset annotations do not change the Unit 3 counter arrangement or its bathroom-door clearance strategy.
The floor-plan deliverable remains valid unchanged; the new annotation behavior is already owned by the separate plan-dimension Requirement.
A separate clause in the same message establishes the hinged-door configuration, which is already represented; the edge-offset annotation change does not alter the door type.
The source asks for the omitted Unit 3 bathroom width but establishes no new width or physical layout value; the edge-offset annotation request does not change its plumbing or fixture layout.
Adding door-offset measurements does not modify the common bathroom's toilet, washing-machine, or drain-alignment requirements.
The dimension-annotation request does not change any wall preservation, demolition, construction, or bathroom-partition policy.
Bathroom-door annotations are unrelated to retention and shared use of the existing main steel entrance.
The source concerns bathroom doors and plan measurements, not the allocation or material of private dwelling entrance doors.
The bathroom-door annotation change has no effect on balcony retention or its conditional enclosure rule.
